frame: glTF / Godot: +Y up, +Z the tank's front (Godot MODEL_FRONT), +X the tank's left; units of the Blender scene

units.note: not yet scaled to the board: one scale for every tank, set against the hex, is still to be chosen

body.rock: rotation.x pitches (negative: nose up), rotation.z rolls (positive: roof toward the tank's right, -X); the pivot is the node's origin, mid-belt, level with the belt tops

turret.yaw: rotation.y, positive turns the gun to the tank's left (counter-clockwise seen from above)

gun.elevation: rotation.x = -elevation: positive elevation raises the muzzle; angles are from the rest pose

recoil.axis: position along `back` (in Mantlet's frame): back along the bore, into the mount

belt_motion: link k lies between path(s) and path(s + pitch), s = k * pitch + distance driven forward (mod length), basis (+X across, outward normal, path direction); wheels turn rotation.x += distance / r

wreck.from: pipeline/wreck_pose.py CONFIG, the sprite wreck's rules

gun.set: rotation.x = +droop: down past the laying limit, to its stop

turret.cant_from: asin(hang below the pivot 0.0000 / ring radius 0.1300 + 0.2898)
turret.pivot: the Turret node's origin: the ring centre at its foot
turret.apply: basis = yaw * tip -- the tip is in the turret's own frame, after whatever yaw it died at; +cant rolls the gun's left down

wreck.belt: the links are laid round the wreck path instead (same count and pitch)

toss.from: the sprite bench's TurretToss: thrown back along the hull, lands on the engine deck and slides to rest
toss.use: pick the landing nearest the yaw the spin brings it to; `at`/`quat` are the Turret node's transform in Body's frame, resting on the deck with the debris gone
